extracted.intended_audience: patent applicants, patentees, and registered patent agents/practitioners dealing with Canadian patent reinstatement, maintenance, fees, and related procedures
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance on reinstating Canadian patent applications deemed abandoned, the due care standard for reinstatement, third-party rights, and detailed rules and procedures for patent-related fees, payments, refunds, waivers, and service standards.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reinstatements Requiring Determination of Due Care
rubrics_metrics.description: Certain reinstatements require a positive determination by the Commissioner that the failure occurred in spite of the due care required by the circumstances (paragraph 73(3)(b) of the Patent Act and section 135 of the Patent Rules).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specifically includes failure to pay the maintenance fee (73(1)(c)) and failure to request examination or pay the examination fee when the reinstatement request is received more than six months after the prescribed date to request examination (73(1)(d)). Such requests should be accompanied by a statement of the reasons for the failure which led to abandonment. See Section 9.04 for application of the due care standard.

rubrics_metrics.name: Time Period for Reinstatement
rubrics_metrics.description: Once a patent application is deemed abandoned, the applicant has 12 months to reinstate the application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples provided illustrate how the deemed-abandonment date and the 12-month reinstatement period are computed in different notice and due date scenarios (examiner’s requisition, maintenance fee deadlines with Commissioner’s notice, section 65 notices).

rubrics_metrics.name: Single Request for Reinstatement for Multiple Abandonments
rubrics_metrics.description: If an application is deemed abandoned for multiple failures, a single request to reinstate may be made.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A reinstatement fee must be paid in respect of each failure and all actions must be taken to rectify all failures that caused the abandonments. For multiple failures handled in a single request, the reinstatements must be made before the end of the first reinstatement period applicable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Due Care Standard — Scope of Application
rubrics_metrics.description: Amendments implementing the Patent Law Treaty introduce a due care standard required for reinstatement after (a) failure to pay a maintenance fee and late fee; and (b) failure to request examination (or pay exam fee) when request is received after 6 months from prescribed date.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Subject to transitional provisions, the Commissioner must determine that the failure occurred in spite of the due care required by the circumstances before reinstatement can be granted.

rubrics_metrics.name: Transitional Provisions for Due Care
rubrics_metrics.description: Failures that occurred prior to October 30, 2019 are not subject to the due care standard.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Section 73 of the Patent Act as it read immediately before October 30, 2019, applies to reinstatement requests for failures prior to that date.

rubrics_metrics.name: Determination of Due Care by the Commissioner
rubrics_metrics.description: The applicant must provide the reasons for the failure to take the action that should have been taken to avoid abandonment; the Commissioner will reinstate if requirements of paragraph 73(3)(a) are met and the Commissioner determines failure occurred in spite of due care.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Commissioner informs the applicant of the determination. The applicant’s provided reasons are central to the decision.

rubrics_metrics.name: The Due Care Assessment Test
rubrics_metrics.description: Commissioner assesses whether the applicant took all measures that a reasonably prudent applicant would have taken given the particular circumstances, and despite those measures, the failure occurred.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Measures taken after the failure occurred will not be considered. Approach is consistent with CIPO acting as a Receiving Office for PCT restoration of priority requests (paragraph 166M of Receiving Office Guidelines).

rubrics_metrics.name: Contents of Request for Reinstatement — Failure to Pay Maintenance Fee
rubrics_metrics.description: To reinstate after failure to pay a maintenance fee and late fee, within 12 months an applicant must: make a request for reinstatement, state the reasons for the failure (to pay prescribed maintenance fee and late fee referred to in the notice) before the later of end of six months after maintenance fee due date and end of two months after date of notice, take the action that should have been taken to avoid abandonment, and pay the prescribed fee for reinstatement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These requirements mirror paragraph 73(3)(a) of the Patent Act and refer applicants to CIPO’s Patent Fees page for invoice of fees.

rubrics_metrics.name: Contents of Request for Reinstatement — Failure to Request Examination (>6 months)
rubrics_metrics.description: If the reinstatement request is submitted more than six months after the prescribed time to request examination, to reinstate within 12 months the applicant must: make a request for reinstatement, state the reasons for the failure to request examination and pay the examination fee and late fee within two months of the date of the notice, take the action that should have been taken to avoid abandonment, and pay the prescribed reinstatement fee.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These are the requirements set out in paragraph 73(3)(a) of the Patent Act for late requests for examination.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recommended Information to Include with the Reinstatement Request
rubrics_metrics.description: To assist determination of due care, the Patent Office recommends including: the circumstances that led to the failure; the measures the applicant took to avoid the failure (including remedial/alternative steps); and any other justifications.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants may include evidence such as medical notes or affidavits. See privacy guidance in Chapter 8.02.05a.

rubrics_metrics.name: Office Procedure — Determination Process
rubrics_metrics.description: The Commissioner will review the reasons provided to decide whether the failure occurred in spite of the due care required by the circumstances.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Commissioner considers whether anything else could reasonably have been done to avoid the failure, taking into account particular circumstances. Measures after the failure are not considered. Consideration will include customary diligence a prudent party would have exercised and have regard to factors used by the International Bureau and Receiving Offices (paragraph 166M), while acknowledging each case is fact-specific.

rubrics_metrics.name: Circumstances That May Favour a Due Care Determination
rubrics_metrics.description: Certain external or unexpected events generally support a finding that due care was taken.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: Force majeure (hurricane, volcanic eruption, earthquake, war); unexpected illness or urgent treatment preventing communication; facsimile or software submission failure due to external technical problem where alternatives were exhausted; unexpected/unforeseeable docketing system error; isolated human error by an assistant in docketing/monitoring/preparation/filing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Circumstances That May Not Favour a Due Care Determination
rubrics_metrics.description: Certain internal or preventable circumstances usually weigh against finding due care was taken.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: lack of financing; human error due to increased workload, lost file, or lack of organization/diligence; lack of knowledge of the Canadian Patent Act and Patent Rules; absence from office (planned vacation or medical appointment) causing missed deadlines.

rubrics_metrics.name: Office Procedure — Observations Before Determination
rubrics_metrics.description: Before making a determination under paragraph 73(3)(b), the Patent Office will send a letter informing the applicant of the Commissioner’s intended determination and provide opportunity to make observations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicant is given until the end of one month after the date of the letter to make observations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Office Procedure — Service Standard for Reinstatement Requests
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicants can expect a response to a reinstatement request, including the Commissioner’s due care determination, within six months of receipt of the request or six months from receipt of the last correspondence relating to the request.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Exception: if applicant is informed that Commissioner intends to determine that due care was not taken, timelines may differ.

rubrics_metrics.name: Third Party Rights When Patent Rights Are Uncertain
rubrics_metrics.description: Third parties who, while patent rights are uncertain, take actions in good faith that would otherwise constitute infringement may be afforded rights and protections under specific circumstances.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Failure to pay a maintenance fee or failure to request examination and pay the prescribed fee could give rise to third party rights (section 55.11 of the Patent Act and section 128 of the Patent Rules). See related sections for details.

rubrics_metrics.name: Tariff of Fees — Official Source
rubrics_metrics.description: Fees relating to patent applications, patents and related services are listed on CIPO’s Patent Fees webpage; the Tariff of Fees in Schedule 2 of the Patent Rules does not reflect current fee amounts for all fees.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consult CIPO’s Patent Fees webpage as the official source for current fee information. References to extensions of time for fee payments appear in other sections (2.03.03g/h/i).

rubrics_metrics.name: PCT Schedule of Fees
rubrics_metrics.description: WIPO oversees treaties such as the PCT; PCT fees paid during the international phase (transmittal, search, international filing) are payable to the receiving office; upon national phase entry, the basic national fee is payable to the national IP office.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consult CIPO’s website and Chapter 34 for more information on PCT fees and schedule of fees.

rubrics_metrics.name: Amount Due — General Rule
rubrics_metrics.description: The amount due for a fee generally depends on the date the Commissioner receives the complete fee payment, not the date the service was requested nor the prescribed payment date.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Fee amounts are adjusted annually; if payment is received before Jan 1 you pay current-year fee, on/after Jan 1 you pay adjusted next-year fee. Exceptions exist for top-up fees and certain international application fees. This rule applies to maintenance fees, early/late/reinstatement payments, etc.

rubrics_metrics.name: Partial Payments
rubrics_metrics.description: If a fee is paid in two or more partial payments, the amount of the fee to be paid is the amount that would be payable if the full amount had been paid on the day the last partial payment is received.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Exceptions exist for partial payments in the form of authorized top-up fees for which an extension must be granted; consult sections 2.03.03g/h/i to identify top-up fee payment rules.

rubrics_metrics.name: Request for Examination — Amount Due Rules
rubrics_metrics.description: The examination fee amount is the amount payable on the day the request for examination is made and the fee is paid; if request and payment occur on different days, the amount due is the fee amount on the later of those days.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If initial payment was insufficient to cover excess claims and the applicant later amends to reduce claims, the total examination fee due is the amount owing on the date of the amendment, which may differ from the original payment date (see 11.01.01 and section 83.1 of Patent Rules).

rubrics_metrics.name: Exception — Amount Due for International Application Fees
rubrics_metrics.description: For certain international application fees (transmittal fee, international filing fee including excess pages/electronic reductions, search fee), the fee amount is the amount payable as of the date of receipt of the international application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This contrasts with the general 'amount due' guidance which uses date of receipt of payment by Commissioner for domestic fees.

rubrics_metrics.name: Small Entity Fees — Eligibility and Declaration
rubrics_metrics.description: Certain fees are reduced for small entities (small businesses and universities). To pay the small entity rate, the applicant/patentee must be eligible under the definition of small entity and submit a signed small entity declaration.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Small entity status is determined at the filing date or national phase entry date. If a standard fee was paid prior to timely small entity declaration, the standard fee remains applicable and no refund is provided for the difference for that payment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition of Small Entity
rubrics_metrics.description: A small entity employs fewer than 100 employees or is a university; it does not include entities controlled by or having transferred/license obligations to entities (other than universities) with 100+ employees.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Status is fixed at filing or national phase entry date; later growth of the entity does not change status for that application.

rubrics_metrics.name: Small Entity Declaration — Who May Sign and Requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: A signed small entity declaration can be included in the petition or as a separate document and may be signed by the single applicant, any one of joint applicants, current patentee (or one of joint patentees), a patent agent appointed on behalf of applicant/patentee, or a registered foreign practitioner authorized by applicant/patentee (with authorization document).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The declaration must indicate name of applicant/patentee and, if applicable, the signing agent/practitioner. A small entity declaration tool is available. Deadline for submission is the relevant fee deadline; late declarations do not trigger refunds where a standard fee was already paid prior to the deadline.

rubrics_metrics.name: Paying Fees — General Requirements and Methods
rubrics_metrics.description: Payments to CIPO must be made in Canadian dollars; payment methods include cheque, credit card, electronic payment service (requires activation code) and others described on CIPO site. Financial information must be provided with every payment and general correspondence rules observed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: CIPO provides a Fee Form to facilitate payment and protect client financial information. See practice notice 'CIPO Fee Payment Practice' (effective June 8, 2009).

rubrics_metrics.name: Deposit Accounts
rubrics_metrics.description: Clients may open Deposit Accounts to load funds from which the Office may withdraw amounts upon client request to fulfill patent lifecycle requirements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Detailed instructions for opening, replenishing and using deposit accounts are on CIPO’s website.

rubrics_metrics.name: Fee Form — Use and Confidentiality
rubrics_metrics.description: Use of CIPO’s Fee Form is strongly recommended for mail, fax, or in-person payments to facilitate processing and secure financial information.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Fee Form should accompany written communications concerning fees; it will not be part of the patent application file open to public inspection and will not be viewable in the Canadian Patent Database.

rubrics_metrics.name: General Authorization Statements for Debiting Fees
rubrics_metrics.description: In limited situations where a payment deficiency/shortfall occurred, general authorization statements in timely client communications may provide recourse to charge balances or fees from a deposit account when there was a clear and obvious intent to pay.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Such statements cannot be used for speculative or conditional situations beyond the specific context. Example: explicit instruction to debit missing request for examination fee will allow debit, but absence of explicit instruction to pay maintenance fee means Office will not debit it. Conditional reinstatement requests cannot be acted upon unless the complete actions required were undertaken.

rubrics_metrics.name: Date of Payment — Rule
rubrics_metrics.description: The date a payment is received by the Commissioner is the date of physical delivery to the Patent Office or the date of receipt at the local time of the Patent Office if delivered electronically.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For partial payments, the date used to establish when a fee was paid is the date the Patent Office received the complete fee. Exceptions exist for deemed dates of payment for top-up fees and partial request for examination scenarios (see related sections).

rubrics_metrics.name: Date of Request for Examination — Insufficient Excess Claims Fee and Subsequent Amendment
rubrics_metrics.description: If initial examination payment was insufficient to cover excess claims and a subsequent amendment reduces claims such that payment is sufficient, the amount paid is considered received on the day the amendment was made.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See sections 11.01.01 and 10.01.02b for cross-reference.

rubrics_metrics.name: Refunds — Types, Conditions, and Time Limits
rubrics_metrics.description: Commissioner will issue refunds following a written request if permitted by subsection 139(1) of the Patent Rules. A list of refundable fee types/conditions is provided (e.g., fees for withdrawn applications within 14 days, registration fees where document not submitted, certain maintenance/exam/final fees paid in the context of abandonment/reinstatement outcomes, overpayments, etc.).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Refund requests under paragraphs 139(1)(b)–(h) must be received within three years of the day the fee was paid (subsection 139(2)). Maintenance fees paid in advance are generally not refundable except where provided under paragraph 139(1)(b). Fees required to be remitted under the Service Fee Act are not eligible for refund (subsection 139(3)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Waiver of Fees — General
rubrics_metrics.description: The Commissioner may waive payment of fees for certain requests (e.g., request of correction under subsection 109(1), request to reissue a patent under section 47, or apply for an extension of time when examiner’s report was delayed).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Waivers are discretionary and require the Commissioner to be satisfied that circumstances justify the waiver. See subsections in Chapter 10 for specifics.

rubrics_metrics.name: Waiver of Fees — Correction or Reissue Request
rubrics_metrics.description: To waive the fee for requesting a correction or reissue, the correction/reissue must be the result of an error by the Commissioner and the Commissioner must be satisfied circumstances justify the waiver.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants are encouraged to request waiver with their correction/reissue request and provide justification explaining how error resulted from the Commissioner. If the Commissioner agrees and fee was paid, it will be refunded automatically; if fee not provided and waiver not granted, fee will be requested before proceeding.

rubrics_metrics.name: Waiver of Fees — Extension of Time for Delayed Receipt of Examiner’s Report
rubrics_metrics.description: Fee for requesting extension of time may be waived if: the examiner’s report was received by the applicant more than one month after it was sent; the applicant applies for the extension within 14 days after receipt; and the applicant provides evidence satisfactory to the Commissioner of the date of receipt.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Under these circumstances, Commissioner may extend reply period to a maximum of 6 months from date of receipt. If requirements are met but no justification is provided, extension will be 4 months. Extensions beyond 4 months require justification and payment of the extension fee.

rubrics_metrics.name: Waiver of Fees — Top-up Amount Due to Erroneous Information (subsection 3(4))
rubrics_metrics.description: If an applicant/patentee relied on erroneous payment information provided by the Commissioner, the Commissioner may waive payment of the difference between amount paid and the amount that should have been paid on the relevant day.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: To waive payment the Commissioner must consider that requiring the statement/application under paragraph 3(4)(c) is not justified and that the circumstances justify the waiver (subsection 139.1(1)). This top-up would not require action by applicant/patentee in effect.

rubrics_metrics.name: Waiver of Fees — Additional Transitionary Top-up Waiver
rubrics_metrics.description: Where payment was waived based on erroneous information, the Patent Rules allow a 4-month transition period in which applicants/patentees can benefit from an extension of time without action if the same erroneous information was provided, the payment period has not expired, and the Commissioner considers circumstances justify waiver.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is provided under subsection 139.1(2) and applies in specified circumstances to allow a short transition benefit.

rubrics_metrics.name: Client Service Standards
rubrics_metrics.description: CIPO commits to delivering administrative services efficiently without compromising quality and timeliness; service standards reflect current levels of service and the goal is to meet targets 100% of the time given the Service Fee Act.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consult CIPO’s website for specific client service standards and performance targets.
